description: §17.1 structural absence for an if= subtree that CARRIES WIRING — an interpolation, an event handler on the if= element itself, and a bind:value input. This is the shape that used to lower to `data-scrml-bind-if` -> `style.display` instead of mount/unmount: any one dynamic descendant flipped `if=` from removes to hides, and 101 of 149 if= sites in the flagship app took that path. @open seeds false and nothing flips it, so #panel, #lbl and #field must all have count 0 — the element does not exist in the DOM, it is not merely hidden. Companion to reactive-if-top-level-absent, which pins the same claim for a subtree with nothing dynamic in it; the two together are the whole discriminator that used to decide `if=` semantics.
rationale: §17.1: "When `expr` evaluates to false, the element is NOT rendered. It does not exist in the DOM." §17.2 draws the contrast: "`show=` hides, `if=` removes". No sentence anywhere in SPEC sanctions a display lowering for `if=` — the only `display:none` sanction is §17.2's, scoped to `show=`. The absence claim is therefore independent of what the subtree contains, and asserting it on the wiring-bearing shape is what closes the hole: before this case, §17.1's "does not exist in the DOM" had no assertion anywhere in the corpus, which is exactly why two divergent lowerings coexisted green.
